note: Made by Obay's second method (see "method"): the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning, 10 picture ideas are written for each ("sections"), the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye. Each scene is made wide (1920x1088) and tall (1088x1920) from the same description and starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. Pictures already used in the chapters beside this one are not repeated, and the important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: When we sin we are not left to face it alone. Jesus speaks up for us before the Father, and he himself has paid for our sins, and for the whole world's.
ideas: In a courtroom a lawyer stands with a hand on the shoulder of a man whose head is bowed
A big brother steps in front of his little brother and pays the neighbour for the broken window
A man walks free through open courthouse doors into daylight
A stranger pays at the checkout for a mother who cannot
A big sister speaks up for her brother at the head teacher's desk
One friend stands up beside the accused when everyone else stays seated
A father pays the shopkeeper for what his son broke
A team captain takes the blame before the coach for a younger player's mistake
A man steps calmly between a boy and an angry crowd
A hand pushes a paid bill back across a counter

sections.meaning: Knowing God shows in doing what he says. Saying is not living: whoever belongs to him walks the way Jesus walked.
ideas: A man raises one hand in a promise and crosses his fingers behind his back
A boy gives a thumbs-up at the door of a bedroom that is still in chaos
A young man carries an old neighbour's groceries up her steps
A small child walks in deep snow, stretching to step in the big footprints ahead
Bare feet step into footprints left on the sand
A hiker puts her feet exactly where the guide stepped on a steep ridge
A man in spotless running clothes asleep on the sofa
A girl waits at the kerb holding her little brother's hand, just as she was told
A teenage boy washes the family car as his father asked while his friends call him away
An apprentice copies every movement of the craftsman's hands

sections.meaning: The command to love is as old as the message itself, and as new as the morning: the darkness is already passing and the true light is shining.
ideas: A hand draws back a curtain and morning floods a dark room
A grandmother and her grandson watch the first light break over a town still half in night
A worn, much-read old book and reading glasses on an old armchair
Street lamps still burn along a street as the sun comes up behind it
A grandfather fastens his own old watch on his grandson's wrist
A night-shift worker walks home as the sun rises
A door is opened at dawn to a brother standing on the step
An old tree covered in fresh spring leaves
Light crosses the bed as a child wakes
Snow melts off a roof in the morning sun

sections.meaning: Hating your brother leaves you in the dark, blind and lost. Loving him is living in the light.
ideas: Two grown brothers sit at opposite ends of a porch bench in deep shade, turned away from each other
One brother stands in the sun holding out a hand, the other sits in the shade turned away
Two grown brothers embrace on a porch in full daylight
A man feels his way alone down an unlit road in night fog
A man gropes along a pitch-dark hallway, a chair knocked over at his feet
A man sits alone in a dark room with the curtains shut while his family eats in the sunny garden outside
A woman with a lantern lights the path for an old man
Two neighbours mend the fence between them in the morning sun
A man walks away from the lit windows of his brother's house into a dark lane
Two brothers repair a car together in bright daylight

sections.meaning: John cheers the whole family on, young and old: you are forgiven, you know the Father, you are strong and have overcome.
ideas: A grandfather, a father and a small boy sit together on the front steps
Four generations of one family walk along a sunny path together, laughing
A small child sleeps on his father's shoulder
A young man walks upright and steady into a storm wind
A grandfather teaches his grandson to fish at dawn
A coach rests a hand on a young runner's shoulder after a hard race
A family reads a letter aloud together at the table
A young man shakes his head and walks away from a crowd that beckons him
Three generations stack their hands one on another
A boy rides on his father's shoulders with his grandfather walking beside them

sections.meaning: Do not give your heart to the world. What it offers dazzles, but it is passing away; whoever does what God wants lasts forever.
ideas: A man stares through showroom glass at a gleaming sports car
The same kind of car, abandoned and rusting in a field
A woman sits among shopping bags looking empty
A man polishes his trophies in an empty house
A child's sandcastle is taken by the tide
A fairground at night, then its litter at dawn
A wilted bouquet beside a mirror
A man gazes through the gates at a mansion
Fireworks fade above a crowd
An old man plants a tree with his grandchild

sections.meaning: Time is short, and some who were with us have walked away. Their leaving showed they never truly belonged.
ideas: An hourglass with its last sand running out
A farming family hurries in the last of the harvest as dusk and storm clouds close in
One empty chair pushed back from a set table, the door left open to the night
Friends sit round a campfire while one walks off into the dark
A man slips out of the back of a gathering with his coat
A gap in a row of choir singers
One shirt left on the bench after the team has gone out
A family at their door watches a figure walk off down the street at dusk
The last light of sunset over a town
A wedding ring left on the table by the door

sections.meaning: You already know the truth, so you can spot the lie. The lie is that Jesus is not the Christ: turn the Son away and you lose the Father, hold to the Son and you have the Father too.
ideas: A glass of clear water beside a glass of muddy water
An old woman at a market gently pushes back a glittering fake, not fooled for a moment
A father opens his front door wide to the friend his grown son has brought home
A father teaches his son's friend to fish, right beside his own son
A mother picks out her own child at once among children all dressed the same
A child turns at her mother's voice in a crowd
A man turns his back on the son and so walks past the father's open door
Faces of every age lit by the same morning light
A baker cooks by heart with the recipe book closed
A father's arms around both his son and his son's friend

sections.meaning: Hold on to what you heard from the start and let no one pull you away. The truth lives in you and keeps you in him, and his promise is life forever.
ideas: The clasped hands of an old married couple, wedding rings worn thin
A grandmother sings a baby the lullaby her own mother sang to her
An old couple dance in their kitchen to the song they first danced to
A small boy holds fast to his father's hand in a rushing station crowd
A compass held steady in an open hand where a trail forks in the mist
A climber clipped to the rope stands steady on a ledge
A family rests under a great old tree beside a river
A grandfather reads a worn storybook to the child on his knee
A child learns to ride a bicycle with her father's hand on the saddle
A lamp kept burning in a window all night

sections.meaning: Stay in him, so that when he comes you can meet him gladly, with nothing to hide. Those born of him do what is right, as he does.
ideas: A boy kneels at the front window watching the road with eager joy
A young apprentice stands glad beside his finished work as the master walks in
A small boy runs to the front door with his arms wide open
A father and his small son walk side by side with the very same stride
A girl stands on tiptoe at the airport arrivals gate
A child hides behind the sofa when his father comes home
A girl holds her finished painting out to the teacher coming back into the room
The lights are on and the table is laid as the family car pulls in
A bride stands ready and radiant at the window
A young gardener shows the returning owner a garden in full bloom

scenes.principle: When we sin, Jesus speaks up for us before the Father, and he himself has paid for it.
scenes.shows: A big brother steps in front of his little brother and pays the neighbour for the broken window.
scenes.prompt: On a suburban front lawn a teenage boy of about sixteen stands in front of his little brother, about seven, with one arm stretched back protectively across him, and with the other hand holds out his own wallet to an annoyed older neighbour. Behind the neighbour a house window is broken, and a football lies on the grass. The little brother peers out from behind his big brother, head lowered. Bright midday daylight.

scenes.principle: Saying we know him is not the same as doing what he says.
scenes.shows: A boy gives a thumbs-up at the door of a bedroom that is still in chaos.
scenes.prompt: A boy of about eight stands in the doorway of his bedroom, facing us with a big confident grin and a thumbs-up, as if the tidying is all done. Behind him the room is in complete chaos: clothes all over the floor, toys everywhere, an unmade bed, drawers hanging open. Bright daylight from the bedroom window.

scenes.principle: Whoever belongs to him walks the way Jesus walked.
scenes.shows: A small child walks in deep snow, stretching to step in the big footprints ahead.
scenes.prompt: A small child of about five in a red winter coat walks through deep fresh snow behind an adult, stretching each leg wide to step exactly into the big footprints left ahead. Only the adult's legs and boots are seen, walking on ahead, and a line of deep footprints leads from them back to the child. The child looks down, concentrating hard. Bright, clear winter daylight.

scenes.principle: The command to love is old, and new like the morning: the darkness is passing and the true light is shining.
scenes.shows: A grandmother and her grandson watch the first light break over a town still half in night.
scenes.prompt: A grandmother and her small grandson sit side by side on a hilltop bench, seen from behind, watching the first light of the sun break over a wide valley town. Below them much of the town is still in blue night shadow with street lamps still on, while the far side is already lit gold and the light is spreading toward them. The boy points at the light.

scenes.principle: Hating your brother keeps you in the dark; loving him is living in the light.
scenes.shows: One brother stands in the sun holding out a hand, the other sits in the shade turned away.
scenes.prompt: Two grown brothers on the front porch of a house in the morning. One stands in full warm sunlight at the porch steps, turned toward his brother, holding out an open hand with a hopeful face. The other sits at the far end of the porch in deep shade with his arms folded, turned away, jaw set, refusing to look. A strong contrast between the sunlit half and the shaded half of the picture.

scenes.principle: Whoever hates is blind and lost, not knowing where he is going.
scenes.shows: A man gropes along a pitch-dark hallway, a chair knocked over at his feet.
scenes.prompt: A man feels his way along the wall of a dark hallway at night, one hand stretched out in front of him and the other on the wall, unsure of every step, his eyes wide and unseeing. A chair lies knocked over at his feet. A cold dim light from a far window outlines him, just bright enough to read his posture and his lost face clearly.

scenes.principle: He writes to every stage of life: children who are forgiven, fathers who know him, the young who have overcome.
scenes.shows: A grandfather, a father and a small boy sit together on the front steps.
scenes.prompt: A grandfather, a father and a small boy of about five sit side by side on the front steps of an ordinary house in warm late-afternoon light, relaxed and smiling at one another, in plain everyday clothes. Three generations of one family, equal in the frame. Nobody stands apart, nobody wears white, and nobody else is there.

scenes.principle: The youngest already know the Father.
scenes.shows: A small child sleeps on his father's shoulder.
scenes.prompt: Close view of a small child of about three, fast asleep with his head resting on his father's shoulder as the father carries him through a hallway at home. The child's face is peaceful and in focus; the father is seen only from behind, his shoulder, neck and the back of his head. Soft, even indoor light from a lamp, late evening.

scenes.from: I have written to you, young men
scenes.principle: The young are strong: his word stays in them and they have overcome.
scenes.shows: A young man walks upright and steady into a storm wind.
scenes.prompt: A young man in a plain rain jacket walks steadily forward along an open coastal path straight into a strong storm wind and driving rain, upright and unbowed, his jacket pressed flat against him and the long grass around him bent flat by the gale. He is seen from the front at a distance, his face calm and set. Grey midday storm light under heavy clouds. He is alone.

scenes.principle: Craving what the world shows off, what the body wants, what the eye wants and pride in what we own, does not come from the Father.
scenes.shows: A man stares through showroom glass at a gleaming sports car.
scenes.prompt: Night on a city street. A man in everyday clothes stands close to a brightly lit showroom window, staring with longing at a gleaming red sports car inside, his own reflection faint in the glass. The car and the showroom carry no badges, logos or lettering. Nobody else is there.

scenes.principle: The world and its wanting are passing away. Whoever does the will of God remains forever.
scenes.shows: The same kind of car, abandoned and rusting in a field.
scenes.prompt: The rusted, abandoned shell of a once-expensive red sports car sits in an open field in soft daylight, its paint faded and peeling, wild grass and small flowers growing up through its frame. No badges or lettering on it.

scenes.principle: It is the last hour: the time left is short.
scenes.shows: A farming family hurries in the last of the harvest as dusk and storm clouds close in.
scenes.prompt: At the very end of the day, with the sun almost gone and dark storm clouds building, a farming family hurries to load the last crates of the harvest from a field onto a trailer. The father points at the darkening sky as he lifts a crate, a teenage daughter runs with another, and the mother waves the others on. There is urgency in every figure: the time left is short. The last warm light falls on their faces.

scenes.principle: Some who were with us walked away, and their leaving showed they never truly belonged.
scenes.shows: Friends sit round a campfire while one walks off into the dark.
scenes.prompt: At night a circle of friends of different ages sit close together on logs around a bright campfire, their faces warm in its light, talking and laughing. One man has stood up and is walking away from the circle into the darkness with his back to the fire, already half lost in shadow. A woman in the circle turns her head to watch him go, saddened. His empty place on the log is plain in the firelight.

scenes.principle: You already know the truth, so you can spot the lie.
scenes.shows: An old woman at a market gently pushes back a glittering fake, not fooled for a moment.
scenes.prompt: At an outdoor market stall a slick, smiling seller leans forward holding out a glittering gold necklace to an elderly woman. She, kindly but completely sure of herself, gently pushes his hand and the necklace back toward him with a knowing smile, not fooled for a moment. Bright daylight.

scenes.principle: To have the Son is to have the Father. No one comes to the Father while refusing the Son.
scenes.shows: A father opens his front door wide to the friend his grown son has brought home.
scenes.prompt: Seen from inside the hallway of an ordinary home, over the shoulder of an older man who has just swung the front door wide open and is holding out one arm in welcome. Only his back, shoulder and outstretched arm are visible. On the doorstep in soft afternoon daylight stands his grown son, smiling, with one arm around the shoulders of a friend he has brought home, a slightly hesitant young man who is beginning to smile. Plain everyday clothes.

scenes.principle: Let what you heard from the beginning stay alive in you, and you will stay in him.
scenes.shows: An old couple dance in their kitchen to the song they first danced to.
scenes.prompt: A couple in their eighties dance slowly together in their small kitchen, holding each other close, her head on his shoulder, both smiling with their eyes closed. An old record player turns on the sideboard behind them. Their wedding rings are worn thin. Warm, clear daylight from the kitchen window.

scenes.principle: Let no one pull you away: hold fast and remain in him.
scenes.shows: A small boy holds fast to his father's hand in a rushing station crowd.
scenes.prompt: In a crowded, bustling railway station, people hurrying past in every direction, a small boy of about five holds tightly with both hands to his father's hand and looks up at him with complete trust, calm in the middle of the rush. The father is seen only as an arm, a hand and part of his coat at the edge of the frame. The crowd around them is a blur of movement; the boy and the joined hands are sharp. Bright daylight from high station windows.

scenes.principle: Stay in him, so that when he comes you can meet him gladly, with nothing to hide.
scenes.shows: A young apprentice stands glad beside his finished work as the master walks in.
scenes.prompt: A young apprentice carpenter stands at ease beside a wooden chair he has just finished in a workshop, wiping his hands on a cloth, smiling openly and gladly toward the workshop door as it is pushed open by his master, who is seen only as an arm and shoulder at the edge of the frame. Nothing is hidden and nothing is half done. Bright daylight through the workshop windows.
